$comment: The manifest for one specification. Rename this directory to your specification's short
name and fill this in; a repository publishes as many specifications as the working group
publishes together, and each is a directory under source/ with a manifest.json in it.
Nothing lists them - adding a specification is adding a directory.
Everything here is either identity that no generator can derive, or content for a clause
the tool generates rather than the working group authoring it. See AUTHORING.md for which
Every <PLACEHOLDER> below must be replaced before the first build.

$comment_model: Relative to the repository, not to this file: model/ is shared by every specification here,

$comment_markdown: Beside this file. The prose, the figures and the Profiles are this specification's own, so
they are named relative to the manifest; the model and the outputs are the repository's and
Any key other than 'main' and 'figures' names a clause broken out into its own file, asked
for with source=<key> on the heading in spec.md. 'objecttypes' below is the usual one: in a
specification with sixty types it is the only clause anyone is editing.
$comment_figureGenerators: How a figure's source becomes the SVG the document embeds: the source's extension, or its
exact file name, to a script that renders it. 'update --write' runs each one from the
repository root as '<script> <source> <svg>'; report mode lists what it would run. Both
.ps1 and .sh are run, so the language is the author's choice.
An empty script means the source needs no rendering because it already is the figure. That
is what a .drawio.svg is - the picture and its own editable diagram in one file - and it is
why a repository that draws in draw.io needs no figure tooling at all.
tools/office-to-svg.ps1 ships with this template for a working group whose drawings are in
Visio or PowerPoint. That is a supported steady state, not a stage of a migration: the
Office file stays the source of truth, is edited in the application that drew it, and
'update --write' re-renders the SVG beside it. What it costs is checking - an exported SVG
carries no diagram to read, so nothing compares its shapes against the model. Moving to a
checkable figure later is one line here.
Only 'update' runs these. A build reads the committed .svg and executes nothing, so what
happens to be installed on the machine that builds cannot change what gets published.
$comment_normativeReferences: Clause 2 is generated from this list, and every mention of a designation in running prose
becomes a citation of the matching entry - so 'OPC 10000-3' in a sentence links itself and
an author never writes the link. 'id' is what a [](#ref-<id>) citation names.
The OPC 10000-N parts below are the set nearly every companion specification cites. Remove
the ones this document does not, and add the ones it does; an entry nothing cites is
harmless, but a citation with no entry is reported.

$comment_terms: The Terms and definitions subclause, which appears only where spec.md asks for it with a
'{clause} kind: terms' directive. Sorted as written; keep it alphabetical.
'source' prints as '[SOURCE: ...]' beneath the definition, and links the designation to its
normative-reference entry; write the designation only, without the brackets. Each entry in
'notes' prints as 'Note 1 to entry:', counted from the term - do not write the label, and do
not write 'NOTE', which is the label for a note on a clause.
Define only what this document uses in a sense a reader would not already have from the
normative references - a term copied from OPC 10000-1 is a term that can drift from it.
A directive with no terms listed here is reported, so delete the directive rather than the
list if this document defines none.

notes: This standard adopts adding a PackML prefix to all PackML defined terms that are used in this standard that are also defined by OPC. The <Term> is the terminology defined by PackML. This allows the terminology used in PackML to be easily distinguished from terminology defined in OPC UA.

terms.definition: a concept that defines a collection of associated modules that can carry out one or more major processing activities.
notes: In PackML Unit and Machine are used to define the same thing and can at times be interchanged.

terms.definition: a concept that represents named data element that is used to command, read status, or provide administration of a unit.
a concept that represents a state model of the operational state of a unit.
a concept that represents the mode of operation of a unit, indicating which state model is currently active.

$comment_abbreviations: Clause 3.3. Sorted as written; keep it alphabetical.
$comment_namespaces: The document's own namespace prints without a prefix; every other namespace prints with
the index assigned here. These indices are the document's, not the NodeSet file's - the
two orderings differ and using the file's would silently mislabel every BrowseName in
'update' assigns an index to anything that needs one and reports what it did, so the way
to fill this in is to add the URI with "index": null and let it number them.
